title: The Western Corridor and the Grumeti River
excerpt: The Western Corridor stretches towards Lake Victoria. It is quiet for most of the year and comes alive when the migration crosses the Grumeti River.
body:
The Western Corridor is a long arm of the Serengeti that reaches towards Lake Victoria. It is one of the least visited parts of the park.

## The Grumeti River

The Grumeti River is known for its very large Nile crocodiles. When the migration passes through, usually around late May to July, herds have to cross the river, and crocodiles take their chance. The crossings are generally smaller than at the Mara River, but intense.

## Landscape

Open plains, woodland and gallery forest along the river. Black-and-white colobus monkeys live in the riverine forest. The area also has resident lions, elephants, giraffes and hippos.

## Why visit

- Quiet game drives.
- The migration in June.
- Good combination with central Serengeti.

## Getting there

By road from Seronera (a few hours), or by plane to an airstrip in the area. Some travellers continue towards Lake Victoria and [Rubondo Island](/blog/rubondo-island-national-park/).

## Private concessions

Next to the national park there are private reserves where activities like walking safaris and night drives are allowed.

Read [the migration in June](/blog/great-migration-june-grumeti/) or [plan your safari](/travel-proposal/).
